# ssh-keys

SSH keys are installed into new instances so their owner can log in.

## GET /v1/auth/ssh-keys

Operation `current_user_ssh_key_list`.

List the calling user's `User`-scoped SSH keys. Returns only the caller's own keys; the bound user_id is resolved from the authenticated principal.

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: array of [SshKey](schemas.md#sshkey)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## POST /v1/auth/ssh-keys

Operation `current_user_ssh_key_create`.

Register a `User`-scoped SSH key owned by the caller.

Request body (required): `application/json`: [NewSshKey](schemas.md#newsshkey)

Responses:

- `201`: successful creation, `application/json`: [SshKey](schemas.md#sshkey)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## GET /v1/me/ssh-keys/{ssh_key}

Operation `current_user_ssh_key_view`.

Read one of the calling user's own `User`-scoped SSH keys. This collection is exactly what `current_user_ssh_key_list` returns, so a key the caller can reach through `/v1/ssh-keys/{key_id}` but does not own is not in it. Every such key answers 404, indistinguishably from a key id that was never issued: a `User`-scoped key owned by somebody else, a `Public`/`Silo`/`Tenant`/`Project`-scoped key, and an absent id all produce the same refusal. Root gets no override here: `/v1/me` means the caller, and an operator reading somebody else's key has `/v1/ssh-keys/{key_id}` for that.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ssh_key` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [SshKey](schemas.md#sshkey)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## DELETE /v1/me/ssh-keys/{ssh_key}

Operation `current_user_ssh_key_delete`.

Delete one of the calling user's own `User`-scoped SSH keys. Same ownership gate and same 404-on-everything-else behaviour as `current_user_ssh_key_view`.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ssh_key` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |

Responses:

- `204`: successful deletion
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## GET /v1/ssh-keys

Operation `ssh_key_list`.

`GET /v1/ssh-keys?scope=<public|silo|tenant|project>`, the one ssh-key collection. `scope` names which selector is in force and which owner scopes the listing carries:

* `public`: keys owned by no scope. The only scope an unauthenticated caller may read, and it takes no selector. * `silo` + `?silo=`: keys owned by that silo, and nothing else. Gated on silo membership; a cross-silo probe sees `404`. * `tenant` + `?tenant=`: every key a member of that tenant can use: public, the tenant's silo's, and the tenant's own. Gated on tenant membership; a cross-tenant probe sees `404`. * `project` + `?project=`: the `tenant` union plus the project's own keys. Gated on membership of the project's owning tenant, which is read from the project rather than taken from the caller.

Naming a selector the scope does not use is `400 ScopeNotAccepted`; omitting the one it does is `400 MissingScope`. Neither is ignored.

Paginated per convention 3: `limit` (default 50, capped at 500), `page_token`, and `sort_by`. Only `id_ascending` is accepted, because every keyspace behind this collection is keyed by the key id. The scope and its resolved selector are bound into the cursor, so a token minted for one scope is `400` against another.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | query | no | string (uuid) | Restrict to a single project. |
| `scope` | query | yes | [SshKeyScopeSelector](schemas.md#sshkeyscopeselector) |  |
| `tenant` | query | no | string (uuid) | Restrict to a single tenant. |
| `limit` | query | no | integer (uint32) | Maximum rows to return. Defaults to 50 and is clamped to 500; zero is rejected rather than treated as "default". |
| `page_token` | query | no | string | Opaque cursor from the previous response's `next_page`. Valid only for the query that produced it. A token replayed against a different selector set or sort order, or modified in any way, is a `400`; it never silently restarts the listing. |
| `sort_by` | query | no | [NameOrIdSortMode](schemas.md#nameoridsortmode) | Order the collection is walked in. Defaults to `id_ascending`. Bound into the cursor, so it cannot change part-way through a walk. |

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [ResultsPage_for_SshKey](schemas.md#resultspage_for_sshkey)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## POST /v1/ssh-keys

Operation `ssh_key_create`.

Create an SSH key at the owner scope named by `scope` in the body. The server parses `public_key` as openssh format and computes the SHA-256 fingerprint.

Authorization follows the owner: `public` is root-only, `silo` requires membership of that silo, and `tenant` / `project` require membership of the owning tenant, which for a project is read from the project rather than taken from the caller. A caller outside the named scope sees `404`, never a `403` that would confirm the scope exists.

Returns 400 if the key cannot be parsed or `scope` is `kind: "user"` (use `/v1/auth/ssh-keys`, which binds the owner to the credential), and 409 if the name or fingerprint is already in use within the named scope.

Request body (required): `application/json`: [NewScopedSshKey](schemas.md#newscopedsshkey)

Responses:

- `201`: successful creation, `application/json`: [SshKey](schemas.md#sshkey)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## DELETE /v1/ssh-keys/{ssh_key}

Operation `ssh_key_delete`.

Delete an SSH key by id. Returns 404 when the key does not exist OR the principal lacks ownership for the key's scope: * `Public` — root only. * `Silo` / `Tenant` / `Project` — any tenant member of the resolved tenant (Phase 0 = same-tenant access). * `User` — only the owning user (or root).

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ssh_key` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |

Responses:

- `204`: successful deletion
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
